content.comment_body: Hello. I'm working on displaying counter values from my [product_name] module. Although I've mapped these counters, I can't get their values to show correctly. Previously, I read that displaying counter values might not work because they're in DWord format. Currently, I've connected an analog multiplexer to the counter for webpage display, but this solution seems unwieldy. Is there a better way to solve this?
Welcome to the forum. If your goal is to display the up/down counter value on your website, you just need to transfer the DWord value via Parameter-VM-Mapping to the VM memory.

Thank you for responding quickly. I've already mapped three counters as DWord at addresses 10, 14, and 18. In the web editor, using the private tag option, I selected VW, Block Number 10 (and similarly for 14 and 18), and Signed. Unfortunately, this setup is not working for me. It's my first time creating a web page for my [product_name] module, and I've been experimenting quite a bit.
You don't need to use the VW block type; use VD (unsigned) instead.

Thanks very much for your advice—that solved my problem. Since I have your attention, could you recommend the best way to display temperatures on a web page? I considered using a mathematical instruction block to divide the value by 10. Is that your preferred method, or is there a better solution for formatting values without a decimal point?

With the built-in features of the current web editor, it's not possible to show decimal places. If you know HTML5, you can manually edit the project after it's generated to add one or more decimal places. An updated version of the web editor is expected soon from [company_name], which will let you specify decimal places, but there's no exact release date as yet.
Alright, thank you for all your assistance. Perhaps we'll chat again. Stay safe.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulties showing DWord counter values in their web applications with [product_name] Web Editor, mainly due to challenges selecting the right memory mapping and data type (signed versus unsigned). The inability to natively display decimal points for temperature readings in the current web editor version also limits data clarity. The discussion highlights the need for clearer guidance and more adaptable display options in such tools.
